title: Wheatstone Bridge
short_intro: The Wheatstone bridge is an electrical circuit used to measure an unknown electrical resistance by balancing two legs of a bridge circuit, one leg of which includes the unknown component. It operates on the principle of null deflection in a galvanometer connected between intermediate nodes.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Conditions for balance, galvanometer deflection principles, meter bridge applications, and standard numerical problems involving unknown resistances.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Sensitivity analysis, network reduction of complex bridges, loading effects, Post Office Box applications, and AC bridge generalizations.

prerequisites: Kirchhoff's Current and Voltage Laws (KCL and KVL)
Series and parallel combination of resistors

concept_notes.heading: Principle of Wheatstone Bridge
bullets: A Wheatstone bridge consists of four resistive arms (P, Q, R, and S) forming a closed loop, with a source of electromotive force and a galvanometer (G).
When the bridge is balanced, the potential difference across the galvanometer is zero, resulting in zero current through the galvanometer branch.
The balance condition requires that the ratio of resistances in one proportional arm equals the ratio in the other arm, expressed as P/Q = R/S.

concept_notes.heading: Balanced Condition and Potential Equality
bullets: At balance, the electric potential at the node between resistors P and Q equals the potential at the node between R and S.
Because no current flows through the galvanometer, current through arm P equals current through arm Q, and current through arm R equals current through arm S.
The balance condition is independent of the applied EMF of the source and the internal resistance of the galvanometer.

concept_notes.heading: Meter Bridge Practical Application
bullets: A meter bridge is a practical implementation of the Wheatstone bridge utilizing a 1-meter long uniform resistance wire stretched over a scale.
Two known gaps on a wooden board hold a standard resistance box and an unknown resistance, replacing arms P and Q.
A jockey is slid along the wire until the galvanometer shows null deflection, dividing the wire into lengths l and (100 - l) which act as proportional arms.

concept_notes.heading: Sensitivity of the Wheatstone Bridge
bullets: A bridge is most sensitive when all four arms have comparable resistance values, ideally equal to the square root of the product of the two adjacent arms.
Maximum sensitivity ensures that a small percentage change in the unknown resistance produces a maximum possible deflection in the galvanometer.
End errors in meter bridges caused by contact resistances at the copper strips are eliminated by interchanging the unknown and standard resistances.

derivations.title: Derivation of Wheatstone Bridge Balance Condition using Kirchhoff's Laws
derivations.conditions: Steady-state direct current circuit with galvanometer current equal to zero (I_G = 0).
steps: Apply Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) at junction B: I_1 - I_3 - I_G = 0. Since I_G = 0 at balance, I_1 = I_3.
Apply KCL at junction D: I_2 + I_G - I_4 = 0. Since I_G = 0 at balance, I_2 = I_4.
Apply Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) to closed loop ABDA: -I_1 P - I_G G + I_2 R = 0. Since I_G = 0, this simplifies to I_1 P = I_2 R.
Apply KVL to closed loop BCDB: -I_3 Q + I_4 S + I_G G = 0. Substitute I_3 = I_1 and I_4 = I_2, and set I_G = 0, yielding I_1 Q = I_2 S.
Divide the equation I_1 P = I_2 R by the equation I_1 Q = I_2 S to eliminate current terms: P/Q = R/S.

derivations.title: Derivation of Unknown Resistance in a Meter Bridge
derivations.conditions: Meter bridge wire of uniform cross-section and linear resistivity with balance length l from the left end.
steps: Let X be the unknown resistance in the left gap and R be the standard known resistance in the right gap.
Let the balance length on the meter wire from the left end be l cm. The remaining length is (100 - l) cm.
Let \sigma be the resistance per unit length of the meter bridge wire. The resistance of the left segment is P = \sigma l.
The resistance of the right segment is Q = \sigma (100 - l).
Substitute P, Q, X, and R into the standard Wheatstone bridge balance formula: \frac{X}{R} = \frac{\sigma l}{\sigma (100 - l)}.
Cancel \sigma and rearrange to solve for the unknown resistance X: X = R \left( \frac{l}{100 - l} \right).

formula_sheet.variables: P, Q = fixed ratio arm resistances, R = resistance taken from resistance box, S = unknown resistance

formula_sheet.equation_html: I_G = \frac{E (R_2 R_3 - R_1 R_4)}{\text{Determinant denominator terms involving all resistors and G}}
formula_sheet.variables: E = EMF of source, G = galvanometer resistance, R_1, R_2, R_3, R_4 = bridge arm resistances
formula_sheet.conditions: General network analysis using nodal or mesh equations

formula_sheet.variables: P, Q, R, S are bridge arm resistances

graphs_and_experiments.title: Meter Bridge Null Point Determination
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A schematic layout of a meter bridge with a DC source, key, galvanometer, jockey, resistance box, and unknown wire, showing the balance length l on a 1-meter scale.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The null point indicates the exact physical position on the wire where the ratio of segment lengths equals the ratio of the resistance arms, resulting in zero galvanometer deflection.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Tested via conceptual questions regarding shift in null point when resistances are interchanged or altered.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Galvanometer Deflection vs Jockey Position
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A V-shaped or monotonically varying straight-line graph plotting galvanometer deflection (or current) on the vertical axis against the jockey position l along the meter bridge wire on the horizontal axis, crossing zero at the balance point.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The intersection of the curve with the horizontal axis (zero deflection) identifies the precise balance length. The slope around this zero crossing represents the sensitivity of the bridge.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used to evaluate student understanding of bridge sensitivity and precision of balancing.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Post Office Box Circuit Schematic
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A circuit diagram showing the internal proportional arms (10 \Omega, 100 \Omega, 1000 \Omega), the variable resistance arm, and the unknown resistance terminals arranged in a diamond bridge network.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Illustrates how industrial and laboratory resistance measurements are organized compactly using plug-type resistance boxes.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Frequently featured in PGT descriptive questions and numerical evaluations.

solved_numericals.question: In a meter bridge, the balance point is found to be at 39.5 cm from the left end when the resistance in the right gap is 12.5 \Omega. Determine the resistance of the unknown resistor in the left gap.
solution_steps: Identify given values: l = 39.5 cm, R = 12.5 \Omega.
Recall the meter bridge formula: X = R \left( \frac{l}{100 - l} \right).
Calculate the right-hand segment length: 100 - l = 100 - 39.5 = 60.5 cm.
Substitute the values into the formula: X = 12.5 \times \left( \frac{39.5}{60.5} \right).

solved_numericals.question: A Wheatstone bridge has arms P = 10 \Omega, Q = 20 \Omega, R = 30 \Omega, and S = 60 \Omega. A galvanometer of resistance G = 50 \Omega is connected between the junction of P-Q and R-S. If a source of 2 V with negligible internal resistance is connected across the other two terminals, find the current flowing through the galvanometer.
solution_steps: Check balance condition: \frac{P}{Q} = \frac{10}{20} = 0.5 and \frac{R}{S} = \frac{30}{60} = 0.5. The bridge is balanced.
Since the bridge is balanced (P/Q = R/S), the potential difference across the galvanometer terminals is zero.
State the fundamental property of a balanced Wheatstone bridge regarding galvanometer current.
Conclude the current through the galvanometer branch.

solved_numericals.question: Consider an unbalanced Wheatstone bridge with arms P = 100 \Omega, Q = 100 \Omega, R = 100 \Omega, and S = 150 \Omega. A cell of EMF 2 V and internal resistance r = 0 \Omega is connected across P and S terminals. Calculate the equivalent resistance of the network across the source terminals.
solution_steps: Identify the network topology: The bridge is connected with arms P and Q in series (branch 1), and R and S in series (branch 2), with arm S connected across. More precisely, node A splits into P and R; P and Q are in series along one branch, R and S are in series along another branch.

Since these two main branches are in parallel across the source terminals (assuming standard bridge terminal connections across input nodes), calculate the parallel equivalent resistance: R_{eq} = \frac{(P+Q)(R+S)}{(P+Q)+(R+S)}.

assumptions_and_limitations: Contact resistances at the binding screws and copper strips in a meter bridge introduce small errors, which are minimized by taking mean readings with interchanged resistances.
Heating effects caused by prolonged current flow through the bridge wires can change resistance values due to the temperature coefficient of resistance.
The galvanometer must possess adequate sensitivity; insensitive galvanometers may fail to detect slight deviations from the true balance point.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The balance condition of a Wheatstone bridge depends on the magnitude of the source voltage and the galvanometer resistance.
common_misconceptions.correct: The balance condition P/Q = R/S is entirely independent of the source voltage and the galvanometer resistance.
common_misconceptions.why: At balance, the current through the galvanometer is zero, rendering the galvanometer resistance irrelevant, and potential ratios depend solely on the resistor ratios.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Interchanging the battery and the galvanometer terminals alters the balance condition of the bridge.
common_misconceptions.correct: Interchanging the battery and galvanometer positions does not affect the balance condition.
common_misconceptions.why: The reciprocity theorem ensures that the balance equation P/Q = R/S remains symmetric upon interchanging source and detector branches.

common_misconceptions.wrong: A meter bridge balance point should always be chosen exactly at the 50 cm mark for maximum accuracy.
common_misconceptions.correct: Maximum sensitivity and accuracy are achieved when the balance point is near the center (around 40 cm to 60 cm), but it does not need to be precisely at 50 cm.
common_misconceptions.why: Percentage errors in length measurement are minimized when the balancing length is close to the middle of the bridge wire.

quick_revision: Wheatstone bridge balance condition is P/Q = R/S.
Meter bridge unknown resistance is given by X = R l / (100 - l).
At balance, galvanometer current I_G = 0 and potential at intermediate nodes is equal.
Maximum bridge sensitivity occurs when all four arms have comparable resistance values.
Interchanging unknown and known standards eliminates end errors in practical setups.
